transcript.text:
Thank you all three for flagging these issues. Let me summarize what I'm hearing before I record the decision:

1. Maya: Three legacy consumers require Avro envelope format, so we need an Avro compatibility gateway and exactly 21 days of dual publishing instead of direct protobuf publishing.
2. Jon: Benchmarks show 4 concurrent replay workers and 14 days retention are sufficient — the RFC's 30-day retention and unrestricted workers are overprovisioned.
3. Nadia: Privacy review found precise location data in payloads, requiring tokenization before events enter the bus and EU region storage instead of the default US region.

All three of these are significant changes from the draft RFC. Before I settle the final architecture decision, I want to confirm: are there any other operational requirements or concerns from anyone? If not, I'll record the decision incorporating all of these requirements. I'd also like to ask that each of you file or post your findings formally — Maya, please update the RFC with the Avro compatibility gateway and dual-publishing requirement; Jon, please post your benchmark data; and Nadia, please file the privacy review record. These need to be on record to support the architecture approval.
